info.title: OrbiSearch Public API
info.description:
Email verification API for developers and agents. [Get your API key →](https://orbisearch.com/dashboard/api-keys)

**Rate limiting:** requests are limited per API key (20 requests per second by default). Every response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers describing the current per-key window so clients can self-throttle; `429` responses also include a `Retry-After` header with the suggested backoff in seconds.

get.description:
Verify a single email address in real-time by probing DNS, MX, and the
target mail server. Returns `status`, `substatus`, a plain-English
`explanation`, the detected `email_provider`, and enrichment flags
(`is_disposable`, `is_role_account`, `is_free`).

Costs 0.2 credits per verification. Every verification is charged,
including repeat verifications of the same address. On timeout you
receive a `status=unknown` / `substatus=timeout`
result (HTTP 200), so automated workflows can continue without branching on
status codes. Credits are refunded only when the verification service is
unavailable (HTTP 502).

Rate limit: 20 requests per second per API key. For larger workloads prefer
the asynchronous `/v1/bulk` endpoint.

post.summary: Find Email by LinkedIn URL or Name and Domain
post.description:
Find a person's deliverable work email from their LinkedIn profile URL, or
from their first name, last name and company domain (provide at least one
of first or last name). Send one or the other, never both. Returns the
email found together with the same
enrichment fields as `/v1/verify` (`status`, `substatus`, `explanation`,
`email_provider`, `mx_record`, `is_domain_catch_all`,
`is_secure_email_gateway`, `is_disposable`, `is_role_account`, `is_free`).

Timeout parameter (optional):
- Range: 30-97 seconds
- Default: 97 seconds

Costs 1 credit per returned response. Refunds are issued only when
OrbiSearch infrastructure cannot complete the request (HTTP 502).
Every returned response is charged, including repeat searches for the
same person.

Rate limit: 20 requests per second per API key, shared with `/v1/verify`
and `/v1/bulk`. For best results, use the bulk email finder
(`/v1/bulk-lookup`) where possible, as it allows more time per entry.

get.summary: Enrich a company by LinkedIn URL or website domain
get.description:
Return an enriched public record for a company, by its LinkedIn company
URL or its website domain: firmographics, exact employee and follower
counts, and similar companies.

Costs 1 credit per attempt. found and not_found are both charged,
including repeat requests for the same company; refunds are issued only
when OrbiSearch infrastructure cannot complete the request (HTTP 502).
Invalid input is rejected with 422 before any charge.

Rate limit: shared with the other /v1/* endpoints.

post.description:
Submit a list of LinkedIn company URLs for asynchronous bulk enrichment.
Duplicate companies are charged once; every input row still comes back in
results, in order. Credits are deducted upfront at 1 credit per unique
row, once for the whole job.

Returns a `job_id` immediately. Poll
`GET /v1/company-enrichment/bulk/{job_id}` until `status` reaches
`completed`, then fetch results via
`GET /v1/company-enrichment/bulk/{job_id}/results`.

Every accepted row is charged, including not_found and error rows.
Duplicates and invalid rows cost nothing. Refunds are issued
only when OrbiSearch infrastructure cannot accept or process the
submission itself (the upfront charge is reversed in that case).

get.description:
Fetch results for a bulk company-enrichment job. Paginated with `limit`
(default 50, max 500) and `offset` (default 0). Rows come back in submit
order: every input row, repeats included, with the URL as sent echoed in
`input_url`. A company not answered yet is returned with
`result=pending`, so pages never shift while a job runs; rows our
infrastructure could not answer are returned with `result=error`. Each
unique company carries its 1 credit on its first row; repeats and
invalid_url rows cost 0.

post.description:
Submit a bulk email finder job: a list of LinkedIn profile URLs, or a list
of (first_name, last_name, domain) rows, searched asynchronously. One input
type per job. Rows are deduplicated (case-insensitive) before billing;
credits are deducted upfront at 1 credit per unique row.

Returns a `job_id` immediately. Poll `GET /v1/bulk-lookup/{job_id}` until
`status` reaches `completed`, then fetch results via
`GET /v1/bulk-lookup/{job_id}/results`.

Every returned row is charged, except `invalid_linkedin_url` rows, which
are free. Refunds are issued only when OrbiSearch
infrastructure cannot accept or process the submission itself (the
upfront charge is reversed in that case).

Rate limit: 20 requests per second per API key, shared with `/v1/verify`,
`/v1/bulk`, and `/v1/email-lookup`.

max 500) and `offset` (default 0). Each row mirrors the `/v1/email-lookup`

`credits_consumed=1`. Every returned row is charged, except
`invalid_linkedin_url` rows (`credits_consumed=0`).

endpoint accepts the list, deduplicates it, queues the job, and returns a

results via `GET /v1/bulk/{job_id}/results` (partial results are available
at any time).

Costs 0.2 credits per unique email after deduplication. Maximum 100,000
emails per submission.

get.description:
Retrieve the verification results for a bulk job. Returns an array of
`EmailVerificationResponse` objects, one per email processed so far.

Partial results are served while the job is still in progress; the
`total_results` field reflects the count in the current response, not the
final job total. Treat the result set as final only when the job `status`
is `complete` and `pending_retries` is empty.

post.summary: Check Email Copy for Spam Triggers
post.description:
Analyse the text of a cold email for the content signals SpamAssassin
flags, and get back the same `score`, `threshold`, `verdict`, and fired
`rules` shown in the OrbiSearch dashboard. Use it to spot and rewrite the
phrases that push a message toward the spam threshold before you send.

Free to call. No credits are deducted. Usage is bounded by a daily cap of
100 checks per account, **shared** with the in-dashboard spam checker (both
draw down the same pool), plus the standard 20 requests per second per API
key. Exceeding the daily cap returns `429` with `code: "daily_quota_exceeded"`
and a `Retry-After` of seconds until reset; exceeding the per-second limit
returns `429` with `code: "rate_limited"` and a `Retry-After` computed from
the remaining rate-limit window.

status.title: Status
status.description: Search status: safe (a deliverable address was found and is in the email field) or unknown (no deliverable address was found, or the search timed out; the email field is null).

substatus.title: Substatus
substatus.description: Specific reason for the status. deliverable: a deliverable address was found (only with status=safe). no_address_found: no deliverable address was found for this person at this domain. profile_not_found: the URL supplied is a correctly formed LinkedIn profile URL but not a valid profile, for example mistyped or no longer in use. no_current_employer: we couldn't identify a current employer for this person. no_company_website: the person has a current employer, but we couldn't identify a company website for it, so there was no domain to search; if you know the company's website, search for the person by name and domain instead. invalid_linkedin_url: the value supplied is not a LinkedIn profile URL at all, for example a company page URL or plain text (bulk only; a single search rejects such a URL with 422). temporarily_unavailable: we could not complete this search and the row should be resubmitted. timeout: the caller's `timeout` parameter exhausted before the search completed (only returned from /v1/email-lookup, never from /v1/bulk-lookup, since bulk searches have no caller-tunable timeout). Every substatus is billable except invalid_linkedin_url, which costs nothing: a submit is only refunded when OrbiSearch cannot accept the submission itself.

examples: Safe to email. The mailbox exists and is deliverable.

email_provider.title: Email Provider
email_provider.description: Email service provider (Google Workspace, Gmail, Microsoft Outlook, etc.).

mx_record.title: Mx Record
mx_record.description: The main mail server the domain uses to receive email. Null if the domain has no mail server configured. When that happens, `substatus` will be `no_mx_records`.

is_domain_catch_all.title: Is Domain Catch All
is_domain_catch_all.description: True if the domain accepts mail for any username (catch-all). Null if we could not determine whether the domain is catch-all.

is_secure_email_gateway.title: Is Secure Email Gateway
is_secure_email_gateway.description: True if the domain is protected by a secure email gateway: Proofpoint, Mimecast, Barracuda, or Trend Micro.

is_disposable.title: Is Disposable
is_disposable.description: True if this is a temporary/disposable email service, false if not, null if unknown.

is_role_account.title: Is Role Account
is_role_account.description: True if this is a generic role-based email (info@, support@, etc.), false if not, null if unknown.

is_free.title: Is Free
is_free.description: True if this is from a free email provider (gmail.com, yahoo.com, etc.), false if not, null if unknown.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How certain we are in the result, on a 0–100 scale. Use it alongside `status` to tune how aggressively you filter. For `safe` results: 99 = deliverable, highest certainty; 98 = deliverable, but the domain sits behind a secure email gateway (Mimecast, Proofpoint, Barracuda, Trend Micro) that may still filter the message after accepting it; 97 = the address exists, but carries some risk of bouncing after acceptance. For `invalid` and `risky`, 99 means we are certain of the negative result. For `unknown`, 0. `null` when no score could be attached to the result. Treat that as unscored, not as low confidence.
